question: Does the UPLB record provide reliable waterbody-specific siganid research candidates, and can the full thesis be reused?

source.title: An assessment of the siganid fishery of the Caluangan Lake and Baruyan River in Calapan City, Oriental Mindoro, Philippines
source.author: Marius L. Panahon
source.institution: University of the Philippines Los Baños, Graduate School
source.documentType: Doctor of Philosophy in Environmental Science dissertation
source.access: The official UPLB repository provides the dissertation metadata and abstract, but states that the document is currently unavailable there. It lists the physical holding location as UPLB Main Library Special Collections Section and call number LG 996 2015 E8 P36. No full text, figures, methods chapter or appendices were retrieved.

studyScope.abstractWaterbodySpecificity: The abstract states that the assessment covered the Lake Caluangan and Baruyan River siganid fishery, then says the two named fishes were identified in 'this young lake'. Treat their abstract-level presence as Lake Caluangan candidates only; it does not establish either species in Baruyan River.

reportedTaxa.disposition: Research candidate associated with Lake Caluangan by the thesis abstract; taxonomy match validates the name string only, not the specimen identification.
Research candidate associated with Lake Caluangan by the thesis abstract; taxonomy match validates the name string only, not the specimen identification.

reportedWaterQuality: The abstract says dissolved oxygen, pH, temperature and electrical conductivity met cited DENR Class SC values at different lake and river sections in dry and wet seasons, while sodium chloride, sulphate and total dissolved solids exceeded the cited standard. Numeric measurements and sampling sites are unavailable; this is historical study context, not current water-safety advice.
limits: The abstract gives a study period but no fish collection dates, station list, coordinates, gear, effort or specimen counts.
The two species are explicitly named in relation to the young lake; do not infer Baruyan River occurrences from the broad thesis title.
The cited GBIF Backbone/ Catalogue of Life matches normalize accepted-name strings only and do not verify the thesis identifications or present-day occurrence.
No voucher catalog numbers or specimen-accession crosswalk were retrieved.
The UPLB record supplies no attached thesis file and no item-specific license or public-app reuse terms were verified.
The abstract does not support diet, bait, catchability, current water quality, local fishing rules or safety advice.

followUp.nextAction: Use the listed UPLB Main Library Special Collections holding and call number as a legitimate access lead. If the full thesis becomes available, verify station-level lake versus river records, methods, vouchers, taxonomy and reuse terms before any structured species projection.
